title: Personal notes: batching heuristics, tokenization mismatches, and rollback playbook
body:
Quick context
- Personal scratchpad for recurring patterns I see during PR reviews and on-call when batching + tokenizer issues show up. Mostly heuristics and quick repros to save time next time.

High-level goals
1) Keep latency SLOs while letting batching reduce cost.
2) Avoid silent correctness regressions from tokenization differences or prefix cache misses.
3) Have a one-click rollback path for risky batching/config changes.

Common failure modes I've observed (notes-to-self)
- Tokenization divergence between model variant A and variant B after a small tokenizer update: leads to off-by-one KV cache hits and degraded completions.
- Small-batch threshold tuning that is too aggressive: increases tail latency under headroom pressure (autoscaler + burst).
- Prefix/KV cache invalidation gaps when rolling models with different vocabulary merges.
- Sticky worker hot paths: one GPU gets disproportionate longer sequences and degrades throughput for whole pool.

Quick checks to run in PR review (fast checklist)
- Do unit tests include tokenizer roundtrip for common locales? (en, zh, de) -> run: python tools/tokenizer_check.py --samples 1000
- Is there a change to sequence length distribution logging? Add a quick synthetic: curl -s -X POST "$LOCAL_API/predict" -d '{"prompt":"x" * 2048}' and inspect logs for kernel selection.
- If batching logic changed: run microbench with variety: seq_lengths = [16,64,256,1024]; batch_sizes = [1,4,8,16]; command: scripts/microbench/run_batch_bench.sh --model local-test --out tmp/batch.csv
- KV-cache compatibility: ensure the PR includes a migration note when vocab merges/splits happen. If not, ask for a compatibility flag.

Repro commands I keep using (local slim harness)
- Start local runtime: ./dev/run_local_runtime.sh --config configs/debug-small.yaml
- Synthetic load: python tools/loadgen.py --qps 200 --seq 128 --duration 90 --batch-mode adaptive
- Run tokenization diff: python tools/tokenize_diff.py --model-a ./models/a --model-b ./models/b --sample-file samples/email-headlines.txt

Heuristic: batching thresholds (my current mental model)
- For tail-sensitive routes (chat interactive): keep max_batch_size <= 8, prefer dynamic batching with max_wait_ms <= 10.
- For throughput-optimized non-interactive (embeddings/bulk): max_batch_size >= 32 and larger wait_ms (30-100ms).
- Autoscaler interplay: if pod_concurrency * avg_batch_size > 64 tokens/ms per GPU, raise alert. (approx numbers — confirm with infra)

Rollback playbook (one-page steps for oncall)
1) Identify offending change: PR id or config key. Use /deploy/rollout page to see which rollout introduced shift.
2) Immediate mitigation: pin model route to previous model-version (toggle in console) OR reduce batching aggressiveness (set max_wait_ms -> 2ms, max_batch_size -> 4).
3) If cascade persists, scale out temporarily (add 2 pods to the pool) to avoid throttling while diagnosing.
4) If bug is correctness (tokenization mismatch), revert model or push compatibility shim to runtime that forces re-tokenize on request (expensive but safe).
5) Create postmortem stub: link to incident doc and quick timeline.

Follow-ups / backlog ideas (short actionable items)
- [ ] Add automated tokenization roundtrip check to CI on every model publish (owner: Priya). Jira: INF-590
- [ ] Create a microbench matrix matrix job that runs on PRs touching batching code (owner: Jonah).
- [ ] Add metric: "batch-size-weighted-latency" to Console to detect when a small subset of large-seq requests move tail.
- [ ] Draft an RFC for a lightweight KV-cache versioning header so old cached entries are ignored safely (owner: me).

Notes for future PR comments (copy-paste friendly)
- "Can we add a tokenizer roundtrip test for this change? Seen regressions when subword merges occur."
- "Please include a microbench output for small/medium/large sequence masks — it helps surface worst-case tails."
- "If this is a perf-only change, please include a rollout plan (canary percentages, rollback conditions) in the PR description."

Open questions (brain-dump)
- Should the runtime maintain a lightweight hash of tokenizer metadata per model to auto-invalidate cache on mismatch? Pros: safety. Cons: overhead on every request.
- Can we simulate autoscaler pressure in CI with a synthetic workload to catch interplays between batching and scale-to-zero?

Random heuristics I've learned the hard way
- Never assume histogram buckets for sequence length are stable across datasets; always sample new traffic when changing kernel selection logic.
- During canary, watch both mean latency and 95/99th; sometimes mean improves while 99th balloons (danger).

Notes-to-self for next review
- If PR touches both tokenizer and runtime, escalate to an "apply together" requirement — these have to land in the same deploy to avoid incompat.
- Add a short template to PRs: "Perf impact, Tokenizer compatibility, Rollout plan, Canary metrics"

End of scratchpad.

-- Ethan
